memory_candidates.content: git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check has three per-site widenings spliced inside its non-empty file_scope_arr guard (own-task-directory, engine-written-state allowlist, derived-output-prefix), all placed AFTER a deployed-tree strip and ALL inside the same guard -- meaning every one of them is a strict no-op whenever a task declares no file_scope at all, since the whole Self-Check short-circuits before any splice runs. A mechanism meant to run unconditionally on every phase commit (e.g. a non-blocking staleness backstop) cannot rely on that guard having executed and must independently guarantee its own prerequisite (idempotent re-source via `declare -F <fn>` before falling back to a fresh `source`, rather than assuming an earlier conditional splice already ran).

lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh's piped-invocation detector (Rule 2) is a naive line-level heuristic: ANY line containing the literal substring 'git-commit-scoped.sh' or 'git-commit-phase.sh' AND an unescaped pipe character (not part of ||) is flagged as a hidden-exit-code violation, with no awareness of quoted-string context. A test assertion like `echo "$out" | grep -q "...git-commit-phase.sh:..."` trips this even though no real invocation is piped -- the script name just happens to appear inside the string being matched. Fix: avoid repeating the literal script-name substring in a piped grep pattern inside such a file; a wildcard or a distinguishing message-only substring (without the script name) sidesteps the false positive without weakening the assertion.

Three independent Containment sites in this codebase (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh WORK (h), git-commit-phase.sh's Self-Check, git-commit-scoped.sh's V10) each apply the SAME predicate against a task's declared file_scope, and a per-site widening (engine-written-state allowlist, own-task-directory, derived-output-prefix) must be independently spliced at ALL THREE to take effect everywhere -- a later site's identical widening never rescues an earlier site's drop, because a dropped path is removed from its own pathspec BEFORE being handed to a downstream site. This subsumption-asymmetry pattern (documented in git-staging-scope.md's 'Three Containment sites, not one' section) generalizes to any future per-site widening added to this corpus.

sapience_notes.subject: lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh Rule 2 (piped-invocation detector)
sapience_notes.value: Is a naive line-level string match on the literal substrings 'git-commit-scoped.sh'/'git-commit-phase.sh' plus an unescaped pipe character, with zero quoted-string awareness -- a test assertion whose grep pattern happens to embed the script name inside a string under test trips it as a false positive, even though no real script invocation is piped on that line.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh's three Containment Self-Check splices (own-task-directory, engine-written-state, derived-output-prefix)
sapience_notes.value: All three are placed inside the SAME non-empty file_scope_arr guard, after the deployed-tree strip -- meaning the entire Self-Check, and every widening it carries, is a strict no-op whenever a task declares no file_scope at all. A mechanism meant to run unconditionally on every phase commit cannot depend on that guard's having executed.

sapience_notes.value: Caught a lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh regression in freshly-written test code (test-git-commit-phase.sh's Case 37) that none of this task's own per-phase verification steps had run, because that specific lint was only in Phase 2's verification list, not Phase 3's -- confirming the value of a whole-tree deploy-time gate independent of any single phase's self-declared verification scope.
